title: Liapoldus Gateway plugin traffic boundary
core: A single Gateway Core stores desired plugin configuration in SQLite, exposes Management API, supervises local plugins only in supervised profile and does not serve or proxy public traffic.

caddyPlugin.process: One separate Caddy plugin instance per Gateway in v1; Caddy and Caddy-L4 are built into the plugin, never into Core.
caddyPlugin.configSource: Versioned plugin JSON settings stored by Core and pushed with ConfigApply; the plugin compiles JSON into its private Caddy runtime configuration.
caddyPlugin.l4: Caddy-L4 handles TCP/UDP relay with mandatory conformance; no Go-net fallback.
caddyPlugin.persistentState: ACME/CertMagic state and site releases use the Caddy plugin persistent filesystem; current/previous site release pointers remain plugin-owned.
caddyPlugin.listeners: Caddy plugin opens its own public listeners. Core does not embed Caddy, launch a second Caddy binary or pass public listener sockets.

pluginDataProtocol.call: Generic unary Call carries the existing versioned JSON contracts.
pluginDataProtocol.registration: pluginprotocol Go SDK offers typed capability handler registration without one protobuf RPC per capability.
pluginDataProtocol.pluginToPlugin: Plugins call explicitly allowed peer instances directly over pluginprotocol gRPC/mTLS; Core distributes policy and is not a payload proxy.

activation: Core persists candidate JSON revision and operation in SQLite, pushes it to required plugin replicas, commits the active pointer only after exact acknowledgements and compensates failed partial application with the previous revision.
configuration: User traffic and plugin-specific configuration are never read from SQLite per request; Core serves active in-memory generations.
ha: Core is one instance and Caddy is one active v1 instance; PostgreSQL, S3 and Caddy shared-storage HA are not required.
